To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the H/DX centroid approach does not reflect the difference in protein states and (ii) the difference in deprotonation rates can lead to a misinterpretation of the protein state, if only the centroid approach is used for data analysis.
centroid monitoring of H/DX data can fail to detect differences between protein states, which may lead to misinterpretation of the results.
H/DX-ESI-MS can be a very useful method for the characterization of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach for the calculation of H/DX data that allows a more accurate characterization of the H/DX rates of protein states and, thereby, an improved characterization of the protein behavior.
the development of methods to characterize protein dynamics and to identify differences between states.
the importance of the deuterium profile in the mass spectra to accurately characterize H/DX rates, especially when there are multiple states present in the sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H/DX-MS can be applied for monitoring protein states but the interpretation of data is not as straightforward as it is often suggested.
a change in the protein state is reflected by an increase in the deuterium uptake in the H/DX mass spectra.

the deuterium uptake of a protein state is the sum of the H/DX rates of the protein's constituent residues, which may be different in different protein states, and the deuterium incorporation of each residue is the result of the sum of all the H/DX reactions in that residue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the centroid mass calculation alone cannot be used for a quantitative comparison of H/DX experiments.
the deuterium uptake is a more sensitive parameter to characterize H/DX rates and, thereby, to detect differences in protein conformational states.
the centroid calculation alone is not sufficient to show differences in the H/DX behavior of protein states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
centroid calculation is not sufficient for the analysis of H/DX data and that the full mass spectrum needs to be analyzed.
centroid calculation should not be the sole method used in the characterization of the H/DX behavior of proteins.
, when using centroid calculation for monitoring H/DX, it is not possible to differentiate the H/DX rates of two states of a protein that are not in the exchange equilibrium.
